model: Intelli-Hood IH4 Exhaust Fan / Auxiliary Airflow
equipment_type: Kitchen exhaust / make-up air fan VFD device (Intelli-Hood demand ventilation)
applies_to: Each exhaust fan and auxiliary airflow (make-up air fan) VFD run by a Melink Intelli-Hood 4 system.
summary: On a Melink Intelli-Hood 4 system every exhaust fan and auxiliary airflow (typically a make-up air unit) VFD appears as its own virtual BACnet IP device behind the System Controller. Each device has the same eight objects: run status, VFD fault, a fault reset, maximum frequency, commanded and actual speed, current and kWh. Fan speed is set by the Intelli-Hood from hood temperature and smoke, not by the BMS.
notes: The same object list repeats on every exhaust fan and auxiliary airflow device; only the Device ID differs.
Output Current is not updated for System VFDs; Output Energy is not updated for System and Allen-Bradley PowerFlex 4/40 VFDs.
Actual speed lags commanded speed during VFD ramp up and ramp down; that difference is normal.
To get speed in Hz, multiply the % speed by Maximum Output Frequency (AV 0).
A fan can be hidden from BACnet with its 'Active on BACnet' setting (default Yes for fans).

source.title: Intelli-Hood BACnet Protocol Implementation Conformance Statement (PICS)

integration.summary: Read run status, actual speed and the VFD fault flag from each fan device; add the kWh counter for energy tracking. The BMS can only clear VFD faults (BV 2); speed and start/stop come from the Intelli-Hood.

minimum_points.why: Write Active to clear a VFD fault

minimum_points.why: Speed the Intelli-Hood is asking for, %

minimum_points.name: Fault Active
minimum_points.why: VFD tripped or lost comms with the Intelli-Hood

integration.enable: No BACnet start/stop or speed command. Fans are started from the Touchpad, schedules or digital inputs; use the Virtual Input Module to do that over BACnet.
setup: The System Controller is the main BACnet IP device (default Device ID 654000) and a virtual router (default DNET 654) for the fan, hood controller and virtual module devices; UDP port 47808.

With BACnet Auto Number on (default), the virtual devices are numbered from 654001: exhaust fans and auxiliary airflows (sorted by name), then hood controllers, virtual output modules, virtual input modules.
IP defaults to DHCP. BACnet runs on IPv4 or IPv6, not both; for IPv6 set IP Type to 'IPv4 & IPv6' and BACnet IP Type to IPv6 (multicast scope default ff05).
Settings are on the Touchpad (System Controller configuration) or the web configurator at http://<controller IP>/ih4-configurator.
Check each fan's Device ID on the Touchpad: Status > VFDs, then press the progress bar above the device name.
gotchas: Front ends that send Who-Is without routing only find the System Controller; run a network/router discovery, select the router with the Intelli-Hood DNET, then discover devices again.
The DNET must be unique; another router or BBMD using 654 breaks access to the virtual devices.
Clearing a VFD fault before the cause is fixed can damage the VFD, motor or fan.
Putting BV 2 Reset VFD Fault Out of Service disables it; writes then do nothing.
Output Energy rolls over on every VFD; poll it often enough to catch the rollover.
